skill.name: coverage-analyzer
skill.description: Analyzes Python coverage reports to identify uncovered lines, prioritize critical paths, recommend targeted pytest cases, and compare progress against coverage goals.
skill.summary: Turn Python coverage data into a prioritized, actionable test plan.
skill.author: Atyantik

content.value_statement: Coverage percentages alone do not show which missing tests matter most. This skill turns Python coverage data into prioritized gaps and targeted pytest recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes total coverage and uncovered lines from terminal, HTML, or coverage data.
Groups coverage gaps by file, function, behavior, and priority.
Prioritizes error handling, validation, authorization, edge cases, and integration paths.
Suggests focused pytest cases, fixtures, parameter sets, and test scenarios.
Compares coverage results over time and highlights improvements or regressions.
limitations: Requires an existing Python project and generated coverage data.
Suggested tests still require review against actual behavior and project conventions.
Coverage gains are estimates until the proposed tests run successfully.
High coverage does not prove correctness, security, or complete behavior.

use_cases.title: Close Feature Coverage Gaps
use_cases.description: Find uncovered paths in a changed module and plan focused tests before merging.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Regression Testing
use_cases.description: Rank untested error paths, edge cases, and integration behavior for a release.

use_cases.title: Enforce Coverage Goals
use_cases.description: Compare results with team targets and identify modules that threaten the quality gate.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the current coverage report. Summarize total coverage, files below target, and the five most important uncovered areas.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a concise project overview.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect One Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Review coverage for [module path]. Group uncovered lines by function, explain missing behaviors, and suggest focused pytest cases.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan tests for a specific feature.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Coverage Trends
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare current coverage with [baseline report]. Identify regressions, improvements, and modules at risk of missing the [target]% quality gate.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review changes across releases or branches.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Risk-Based Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Prioritize uncovered error, validation, authorization, and integration paths across [project path]. Propose a staged test plan with estimated coverage impact.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create an advanced plan for broad coverage improvement.

output_examples.input: Analyze coverage and focus on critical gaps.
output_examples.output: Current coverage is 75.3% against an 80% target. Prioritize untested validation errors, empty configuration handling, and API retry failures.

output_examples.input: Suggest quick coverage improvements for validators.py.
output: Add parameterized cases for empty, malformed, and missing values.
Verify expected exceptions and chained causes.
Test unexpected dependency failures without relying on external services.

output_examples.input: Compare this report with last week's result.
output_examples.output: Coverage improved from 72% to 75%, but progress has stalled. The largest remaining gaps are error paths and retry behavior.

best_practices: Generate a fresh coverage report before requesting analysis.
Provide project conventions and the required coverage threshold.
Review recommendations for behavioral value before optimizing the percentage.
anti_patterns: Do not treat line coverage as proof that behavior is correct.
Do not add weak assertions only to execute uncovered lines.
Do not mock internal behavior when real code can run reliably.

faq.question: Which coverage formats can this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It can reason from terminal summaries, HTML reports, .coverage data, and module-level line details available in the project.

faq.question: Does it write tests automatically?
faq.answer: It recommends concrete pytest scenarios and examples. Test creation and execution depend on the requested task and project access.

faq.question: Can it analyze branch coverage?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide branch coverage results so it can identify untested decision outcomes.

faq.question: Can it compare coverage over time?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide current and baseline results, or a coverage history file, for trend analysis.

faq.question: Does it guarantee an 80% result?
faq.answer: No. It estimates likely gains, but actual coverage depends on successful tests and the measured code paths.

faq.question: Is 100% coverage enough to prove quality?
faq.answer: No. Coverage measures execution, not assertion strength, requirement completeness, security, or defect absence.
